English translation from the Modern Amharic of the EOTC Bible (nehemiah-osc.org) by Claude (Anthropic) with collaborator, May 2026. Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication (archive.org/details/three-books-of-meqabyan-cc0-translation). Apparatus integrates Josef Horovitz, 'Das äthiopische Maccabäerbuch,' Zeitschrift für Assyriologie XIX (1905), pp. 194-233 — PD primary scholarly study. 64-citation third-pass audit verdict matrix; 57 verified, 4 errors corrected, 3 interpretive readings flagged, 7 newly discovered parallels added. Dating widened to Aksumite-to-Solomonic Ethiopian Christian range (4th-14th c. CE); precise composition date undetermined in current scholarship per Horovitz 1905 non-commitment. Three books: 1 Mq 36 chapters (Maqabis-of-Benjamin martyrology vs Ṣiruṣaydan); 2 Mq 21 chapters (Maqabis-of-Moab conversion + sons' martyrdom + Ṣiruṣaydan's death); 3 Mq 10 chapters (homiletic + angelological dialogue + Satan-refused-Adam tradition + resurrection-doctrine).
candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 7: direct SECOND-PERSON ADDRESS TO THE KING on the duties of royal office. The chapter's homiletic mode shifts from third-person narrative (chs 2-6) to direct apostrophe — Ṣiruṣaydan is addressed YOU. The argumentation moves from the king's CREATEDNESS (vv. 1-5) to the duty of IMPARTIAL JUDGMENT (vv. 6-14) to the DIVINE MULTIPLICATION OR SHORTENING OF DAYS according to obedience (v. 15). The direct-address-to-king genre parallels: Wisdom of Solomon 6:1-11 ('Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth'); Sirach 10:1-11 ('A wise judge will instruct his people'); Romans 13:1-7 (Paul on the ruler bearing the sword); 1 Peter 2:13-17 (Petrine on submission to civil-authorities). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the brothers themselves voice the address, not a prophet or sage — making the martyrs into the prophetic-instructors of the king who is destroying them.
